 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1988, against respondent seeking compensation on account of grievous injuries sustained by him in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
Gangaiah H.S vs K. Selvaraju on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105339543/
1

On 05.03.2022 at about 05.45 p.m, the petitioner was pedestrian in front of Jayadurga Kalyana Mantapa, near Vijaya Bank, J.C. Nagar, Mahalakshmipuram,
Bengaluru - 560 086, suddenly Car bearing No.KA-17-M-3120 which was driven by its driver at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and suddenly dashed against the petitioner.
Due to this, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Chord Road hospital,
Basaveshwaranagar, wherein he was admitted and after gtiving initial treatment, on 06.03.2022 he was shifted to higher treatment to (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 Aditya hospital, Tumkur and admitted as inpatient from 06.03.2022 to 11.03.2022.
After necessary treatment discharged with an advise for follow-up treatment, not to involve in any strenuous activities and for complete bedrest and still he is continuing follow-up treatment and has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment, regular follow-up treatment every month, travelling and other incidental charges and involved another surgery to IT fracture of left hip non-union on 30.09.2022 and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/-.
As per the advise of the treated doctor inform the petitioner in future days also 2 to 3 surgery is very much necessary to the petitioner.

The injuries sustained by the petitioner has not recovered and is getting unbearable pain often, on account of left hip joint and injuries has not united and getting headache and giddiness often and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature.

Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 54 years and working as Cook in Social Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, Sira, Tumakuru and drawing salary of Rs.40,584/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries, till today cannot attend to (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 his work,
resulted in loss of earning, earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said offending Car by its driver and in this regard the Rajajinagar Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of said offending Car.
The respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with cost and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent did not appeared before the tribunal and hence, he was placed exparte.

04. The following points that arise for my consideration are as under:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 01.

Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have been taken place on 05.03.2022 at about 05.45 p.m, in front of Jayadurga Kalyana Mantapa, near Vijaya Bank, J.C. Nagar,
Mahalakshmipuram, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing No.KA-17-M-3120 by its driver, as alleged in the petition?
Gangaiah H.S vs K. Selvaraju on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105339543/
2 02.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
What order or award?
05. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself got examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed his side evidence.
06. Heard arguments on petitioner side.
07. My answer to the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the affirmative  Point No.2: Partly in the affirmative

Point No.3: As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 08. Point No.1:- PW.1 filed affidavit by stating that, due to the negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-17-M-3120 accident took place and he sustained injuries.
This witness is not cross-examined by the respondent as he was placed exparte.

On perusal of the exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Car the accident was occurred and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.2 FIR registered at Rajajinagar Traffic Police (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 against offending Car driver.
Ex.P.3 is the important document of Investigation Officer.

After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against driver of the offending car as A1 due to his rash and negligent driving and against respondent/owner as A2, for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC and Sections 134(B), 187, 146, 196, 5 and 180 of IMV Act for the reasons that the driver of the car after causing the accident has not informed the accident to the Police and did not taken the injured to the hospital for providing treatment, without stopping the vehicle fled away from the accident spot and the owner has allowed his vehicle to the driver to ply on the public road without insurance.

Ex.P.4 and 5 are the Sketch and Spot Mahazar which shows the accident took place on Kurubarahalli 3rd Main Road, near Jayadurga Kalyana Mantapa, Bengaluru, wherein the offending car came from East to West direction, came to its extreme right side and dashed against the petitioner who was coming from West to East direction as pedestrian on the left side of the road,
which is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is Wound certificate shows petitioner sustained swelling and tenderness present over the left hip joint.
X-ray of left femur shows fracture left neck of femur noted with displacement, said injury is grievous (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 in nature.

Ex.P.7 is IMV Gangaiah H.S vs K. Selvaraju on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105339543/
3 report shows involvement of offending car in the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P.11 and 12 are Discharge summaries shows petitioner sustained IT fracture of left hip non-union and communited IT fracture left hip and L2 compound fracture without neurological deficit.
Ex.P.13 is Aadhaar card of petitioner.
To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent has not lead any evidence, as he was placed exparte.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
09. Point No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 54 years and working as Cook in Social Welfare Department,
Government of Karnataka, Sira, Tumakuru and drawing salary of Rs.40,584/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, regular follow-up treatment every month, travelling and other incidental charges and involved another surgery to IT fracture of left hip non-union and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/-.
Due to accidental injuries, till today cannot attend to (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 his work, resulted in loss of earning, earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.

10. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 Pay slips for the month of February, March, April 2024 which shows that he working as Cook in Social Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka and drawing gross salary of Rs.54,199/- p.m as on April 2024.

entities.text: Social Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In support of his evidence, he has not examined any of his employer.
This document clearly goes to show that petitioner was working as Cook and drawing gross salary of Rs.54,199/-.
11. Reduced disability of employment:- The petitioner herein asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

In order to prove the same,
the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P.7 goes to show that, he had sustained one grievous injury, for which he took the treatment as inpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summary for consideration.
Apart from this, another (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 material witness by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N examined as PW.2.

PW.2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained L2 compression fracture with comminuted fracture of the left proximal femur and he assessed disability to left lower limb at 52% and to the whole body at 17% and he has produced Clinical report and X-ray as per Ex.P.14 and 15.
This witness is not cross-examined by the respondent as he was placed exparte.
12. PW.1 has stated that he was working as a Cook and was getting salary of Rs.40,484/- p.m.

He has produced Ex.P.21 salary certificate shows gross salary for the month of April 2024 is Rs.54,199/-
p.m.
However, it is admitted fact that eventhough he has not cross-examined by the respondent,
now also he is working in the same department and drawing more salary.
From the said facts it is clear that the petitioner has continued his service, still he is getting more salary.

Gangaiah H.S vs K. Selvaraju on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105339543/
4 13.
At this stage it is necessary to rely the decision reported in 2020 (4) KCCR 2621 between Nandeesh K. Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another 14.

entities.text: Nandeesh K. Vs. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., & Another 14
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The principle laid down in the supra decision is that 'unless the petitioner is able to prove (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 that the said disability has affected his earning capacity, he is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earnings'.
15.
In such a situation, question of loss of future income does not arise all.
At the same time, it is to be noted that, due to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, there would be some difficulty to him to do normal work, as he was earlier.
Hence, I relied the decision reported in ILR 2015 KAR 167 in between Dr.Yashawanth Dongre V/s Salman Rasheed and others, it was observed that, "The claimant has got disability to the extent of 46%.

entities.text: Dr.Yashawanth Dongre V/s Salman Rasheed and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctor has not spoken about the disability with regard to the whole body.

The claimant has permanent disability and thus has permanent diminution of his earning capacity, but he has been continued in the same employment without deduction of salary, the claimant is entitled for compensation for his handicap in the labor market.
In many cases of comparatively not serious injuries, though there is some permanent disability, the disability has no immediate adverse effect on his salary.
He may be getting the pre- accident salary.
However, such a man is at a disadvantage when compared with his co-workers in the labour market.

It may so happen (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 that he continues to work with difficulty and gets the same salary but if there is reduction in the workforce by the employers,
this worker with disability is likely to be sent off first."

16. On perusal of the above said decision, it is observed that, though the claimant is in a position to work physically after the accident as before, the after effects of the accident may make it more difficult for him to find work or to retain his work.
There would be some degree of physical handicap.
Since the claimant is continuing his employment, he may be entitled for compensation under the head of reduced eligibility of employment.
In this regard, a suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages, having regard to his disability.

17. In the instant case, on going through the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also on going through the evidence given by the doctor in connection with the disability of the petitioner, I am of the view that, though the petitioner has continued his job, he has to suffer with the said disability throughout his life and the eligibility of her employment has been reduced due to the disability sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.
So, suitable sum has to be awarded by way of damages (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 having regard to her disability.

Considering the above facts, I am of the view that, it is just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under the head of reduced eligibility of employment or damages due to disability.

18. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.11 and 12 Discharge summaries the petitioner was admitted to Manipal hospital, Bengaluru and Aditya hospital, Tumkur, as inpatient totally for 11 days only.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Gangaiah H.S vs K. Selvaraju on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105339543/
5 19.
Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and as per Clinical report and X-ray and on account of accidental injuries
, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
But the doctor has not stated anything about taking rest and he has not produced any documents to prove the same.
As already stated above petitioner He has produced Ex.P.21 salary certificate.
It shows that the petitioner was working as Cook in Social Welfare Department and his gross salary for the month of April 2024 is Rs.54,199/-.
On going through the discharge summaries the petitioner was admitted for 11 days as inpatient.

During the period of treatment,
definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work at least for a period of three months by looking into the nature of the injury sustained by him.

Hence, this tribunal is of the considered opinion that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,08,000/- (Rs.54,000 x 2) under the head loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.
21. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.9 for Rs.5,63,055/- and Prescriptions as per Ex.P.10.
On perusal of Ex.P.9 Medical bills, it is found that Sl. No.2, 3, 4, 5 and 38 are the deposit amount, totalling to Rs.2,02,900/-.
Hence, the said amounts has to be (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.5708/2022 deducted in total amount.
There is no dispute regarding medical bills by the respondent as he was placed exparte.
Hence, after deducting the said amount, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,60,155/- under this head.
22. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
23. Future medical expenses:-

According to doctor PW.2, the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant and the estimate cost is around Rs.60,000/-, but he not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
24. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount in No. Rs.
 1. Reduced disability of employment 50,000-00  2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.5708/2022  3. Conveyance, Nourishment and 30,000-00
Attendant Charges

4. Medical Expenses 3,60,155-00 Gangaiah H.S vs K. Selvaraju on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105339543/
6  5. Loss of amenities in life 30,000-00  6. Loss of income during laid up 1,08,000-00  period  7.
Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 6,38,155-00 25.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,38,155/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
26.
Regarding liability:- As discussed earlier, despite service of notice, the respondent remained absent and placed exparte and he has not denied the case of the petitioner.

It is also admitted fact that the respondent being the RC owner of the offending Car and the Car had no valid insurance policy and hence, he is liable to pay above said compensation amount of Rs.6,38,155/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Point No.2 partly in affirmative.
27. Point No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,38,155/- (Rupees Six lakhs thirty eight thousand one hundred and fifty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent, shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
